articles.title: Giving Community Photos a Second Life
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A neighborhood organization may have years of photographs and still struggle to find a suitable picture for its next announcement. A street-fair photo is too small for print, a workshop picture has harsh lighting, and another carries last year's event date. For groups that run on volunteer time and limited budgets, taking new photographs for every newsletter or campaign is rarely practical. Thoughtful editing can make existing material useful again. Begin with the purpose of the picture Before editing anything, decide what the audience needs from the image. An event announcement should tell people what kind of gathering to expect. articles.title: Fails to Disclose Income During Divorce
articles.author: Sejal Desai
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Divorce requires both spouses to provide accurate financial information so that courts can make informed decisions about property division, child support, and spousal maintenance. When one spouse conceals earnings, understates business income, or fails to disclose financial resources, the consequences can extend beyond an unfair settlement. Deliberate financial dishonesty may lead to court sanctions, additional legal expenses, and the reopening of certain financial decisions. Income disclosure is particularly important when one spouse earns substantially more than the other or controls a business with complicated financial records. articles.title: Catastrophic Injury
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A serious accident can change someone's life in an instant. Whether the incident involves a car collision, workplace accident, medical error, or dangerous property condition, the resulting injuries may require extensive treatment and months of recovery. However, not all severe injuries have the same long-term consequences. In personal injury law, the terms serious injury and catastrophic injury are often used to describe different levels of physical harm. articles.title: Beyond Academic Credentials
articles.author: Britta Hedlund

A prestigious law degree and strong academic performance can help an attorney secure an interview, but they rarely tell the complete story of a candidate's professional potential. Today's law firms increasingly evaluate qualities that extend beyond transcripts, law school rankings, and traditional credentials. Practical experience, communication skills, business judgment, and the ability to build lasting client relationships often influence hiring decisions just as much as educational achievements. articles.title: Drug Sentencing Laws
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Facing a drug charge for the first time can create considerable uncertainty about the future. Individuals with no previous criminal convictions may assume that their lack of a record will protect them from serious penalties. However, drug sentencing laws vary widely, and even a first offense can result in substantial fines, probation, or incarceration, depending on the circumstances. Courts generally consider several factors when determining sentences for drug offenses, including the type and quantity of controlled substance, the nature of the alleged conduct, and the defendant's criminal history. articles.title: Workers’ Compensation Claim Is Denied
articles.author: Sejal Desai
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A workplace injury can leave employees facing medical bills, lost wages, and uncertainty about their financial future. Workers’ compensation insurance is designed to provide benefits to eligible employees who suffer job-related injuries or illnesses. However, receiving those benefits is not always straightforward, and some workers discover that their claims have been denied. A denial can be particularly stressful when an employee cannot return to work or requires ongoing medical treatment. articles.title: Reduce Tire Waste
articles.author: Britta Hedlund
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Drivers can reduce tire waste by preventing premature wear, buying suitable replacements when needed and arranging responsible collection for the old set. Start with maintenance and a clear replacement quote rather than paying extra for a vague environmental label. The aim is to get the full safe service life from a tire, then keep it out of unmanaged waste streams. For a household that relies on a car for work, school or caregiving, an unexpected tire bill can disrupt the month’s budget. Environmental advice has to account for that reality. articles.title: A Fight for Workers’ Rights Turned the Tide in Brazil
articles.author: Cruz Bonlarron Martínez
articles.content_excerpt: As Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his historic victory over far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, he embraced trans congresswoman Erika Hilton and kissed her on the cheek in celebration. The video circulated on social media, with many users pointing to it as evidence of Brazil’s acceptance of trans identity and the key role that the LGBTQ+ community plays within Lula’s coalition. It is important to note that Hilton and other LGBTQ+ politicians are more than simply a piece of a diverse coalition. They are the force behind a piece of legislation that will reduce the Brazilian workweek from forty-four to forty hours, a historic achievement that contributed to Lula’s victory and helped keep fascism at bay. articles.title: Iowa Locals Prevail in Recertification Elections
articles.content_excerpt: Two UE locals prevailed in “recertification” elections covering four public-sector bargaining units in October. The elections are required by the punitive anti-union law passed by Iowa Republicans in 2017. Public-sector unions are required to win votes from a majority of the bargaining unit, not just those voting — a standard that few if any politicians could meet. The law not only requires recertification elections every two years, it also severely limits what unions can bargain over: wages are the only mandatory subject of bargaining — meaning it is the only issue that can be taken to arbitration. Eight years later, DSA boasts more than 120,000 members and politicians in elected offices across the country. articles.title: Life Beneath the Melting Glaciers
articles.author: Jaclynn Ashly
articles.content_excerpt: Bulbul Kaie remembers when summer in Hassanabad revolved around a stream. The village lies in the mountains of Gilgit-Baltistan, a disputed territory in northern Pakistan bordering China, Afghanistan, and Indian-administered Kashmir. Kaie’s family would carry chairs down to the stream fed by meltwater from the glaciers above, where a cold breeze rose from the water. They would spend afternoons on its bank among orchards heavy with apricots and cherries. “We would sit together, drink tea, and enjoy the sound of the stream until it got dark,” recounts the mother of four. “We used to look forward to summer. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Honestly, it’s hard to believe that, once upon a distant time, I was born into an America still fighting a world war. No, it wasn’t World War I! I’m not quite that old! My actual birthdate was July 20, 1944, while World War II was still ongoing. And though it ended in August 1945, in some strange sense, American-style war has never truly ended.
